description: UrbClim is an urban climate model developed by VITO, the Flemish research institute, and the Urban Climate Simulator is its online configurator, which replaced the earlier urban heat island quickscan map service listed on Climate-ADAPT. The site read on 2026-09-28 (version 2.2.4) says the simulator, launched on 3 October 2024, runs UrbClim on VITO supercomputers for any city in the world, any period and climate scenario from 2001 to 2100 and a pre-selected land use specification, at up to 100 metre resolution, and delivers a data package of temperature and heat stress indicators in NetCDF, GeoTIFF and PNG, with optional hourly output and a technical document; custom impact, adaptation cost-benefit and 1 metre studies are offered on request. The earlier quickscan showed results for 102 European urban areas at 250 metres. Coverage is global. Access is a paid service described as low cost; prices and terms of use were not read. Caveats: outputs depend on the land use presets, and the old quickscan maps are archived. It supports heat adaptation studies, such as locating hospital districts with high heat stress. Related record: the Antwerp heat stress case study used UrbClim.
